en: Now, the Phiṭ-sūtras:
"The final syllable of a word ending in phiṭ is acute" (1); "The words *pāṭala*, *pālaṅka*, *ambā*, and those signifying the ocean [are acute on the final]" (2).
The [substitution of *u* for *v*] does not occur after *geha*, *artha*, *asvi*, or *guda*; nor does it occur after a word preceded by *dhi* when it refers to one's own property (*svaviṣaya*).

6. [The suffix *ka*] is applied after words such as *khāta* and *aśman* when they denote something external; 7. [the suffix *ka*] is applied after words ending in *sarat*, *śatha*, and *anta*; 8. [the suffix *ka*] is applied after the word *dakṣiṇa* when it means "skilled."
In the case of a name for one's own limb, the first vowel may optionally be pluta;
likewise in the Veda; and also after *kṛṣṇa*, provided it is not the name of a Ṛg-verse.
Or [the name] of a personal name;

(12) the initial [consonant] of "white" (*śukla*) and "bull" (*gaura*); (13) the final vowel of "thumb" (*aṅguṣṭha*), "water" (*udaka*), "heron" (*baka*), and "cow" (*vaśā*) in Vedic usage; (14) [and so forth].
And [the suffix] *cha* is applied after *pṛṣṭha*,
provided that it is called *arjuna*;
and [the suffix] *ya* is applied after [a word ending in *u*], provided that it is called *svāmin*.
If *āśā* is designated as a direction (18);
if [the name] refers to the constellations (*nakṣatra*) whose objects are the quarters (19);
and if *kṛtikā* is not preceded by *ku* (20).

And [the svarita accent is applied] to *ghṛta* and so forth; [the svarita is applied] to the two words for age, *jyeṣṭha* and *kaniṣṭha*; and the svarita is optionally applied to *vilava* and *tiṣya*.
Thus ends the first quarter in the Phiṭ-sūtras.
The second quarter begins:
"Now, [the udātta accent applies] from the beginning up to the word śakaṭi. (1)
1. For a word ending in a short vowel that refers to a female; 2. for a word not ending in *ni* that does not refer to a neuter object; 3.
and for grasses and grains that have two syllables.

5. [The suffix *ka* is added] after a numeral; 6. [it is added] after words ending in a nasal or a sibilant (*śiṭ*) that do not end in *m*; 7. [it is added] after names of living beings preceded by *ku*.
If it is called artificial (*kṛtrima*), [the suffix *ka*] is applied after words ending in *khaya*,

11. A short vowel is substituted for the final of a word ending in a short vowel when followed by *anṛt* [in the sense of] habituality. 12. [A short vowel is substituted for the final of] *akṣa* when it does not mean "gambling.
13. [A short vowel is substituted for the final of] *ardha* before *asamadyo*.

And [the elision] occurs when the name of the object of comparison (*upameya*), such as "villages" and so forth, ending in the suffix *lu* (i.e., the elided *śas*), follows words meaning "yellow" (*pīta*) and so forth.
Not [the names of] specific trees, mountains, tigers, lions, or buffaloes;
nor that of a specific king, if it has a long vowel at the end, or consists of two syllables, or has many syllables with a heavy (guru) penultimate. 17–19.
20. For words denoting women, objects of sense, colors, and eyes, the shorter [vowel] comes first;
21. and for birds, the lighter [syllable] comes first;
22. and for names of seasons and living beings, [the same applies].
In the case of words for grains ending in *vṛddha* vowels and ending in *kṣ*, 23; in the case of words for inhabited countries (*janapada*) ending in *ś* and *ṣ*, 24;
and in the case of horses and other animals whose final consonants are not combined with *l*, the suffix *matup* is added either after the penultimate vowel or after the final consonant. 25.
"And for those ending in *i* or *u*, [the acute accent falls on the final syllable]," according to Phiṭ-sūtra 2.26; this concludes the second quarter,
and now begins the third quarter.
Now, secondly: (1) [the rule applies] prior to the word *īṣā*;
(2) for words consisting of three syllables, prior to the word *makara*;
(3) for parts of one's own body (*svāṅga*) such as *akurva* and so forth.
And [the groups] beginning with *mā*, 4;
those beginning with *śa*, 5;
those ending in *p* such as *guru* and so forth, 6.

7. The initial vowel of words ending in *yuta* when followed by a suffix with an indicatory letter *ṇ* or *aṅ*, and of the words *makara*, *varūḍha*, *pāra*, *vetasa*, *vitasti*, *ikṣu*, *ārja*, *drākṣā*, *kala*, *umā*, *kāṣṭhā*, *peṣṭhā*, and *kāśī*, may optionally be long.
8. And this [lengthening] also occurs in the Vedic language (*chandas*).
And [the rule] applies to kardama and the others (10),
as well as to sugandhitejana (11),
and to those ending with naptṛ and phala (12).
That which precedes the final consonant of *yānta* (a word ending in *y*) [is long];
likewise for *thānta* (a word ending in *th*), except when followed by *n*, *l*, or a light vowel;
and also in the case of *śiśumāra*, *udumbara*, *balīvarda*, *uṣṭra*, *arapūra*, and *purūravas*.
16. For the [names of] Sāṃkāśyaka, Kāmpilya, Nāsikya, and Dārvāghāṭa, [the suffix *ka* is applied].
17. For a word ending in *īṣā*, provided it begins with *haya* or another such term, the first syllable may optionally be lengthened.
18. [The suffix *ka* is applied] to *uśīra*, *dāśeraka*, *pāla*, *palāla*, *śaivāla*, *śyāmāka*, *śāra*, *ura*, *śarāva*, *hṛdaya*, *hiraṇya*, *araṇya*, *apatya*, and *deva*.
If [the word] *iṣṭakā* follows *mahiṣī*, *āṣāḍhī*, or *ūrjā*, [it retains its original accent].
Thus ends the third quarter in the Phiṭ-sūtras;
here begins the fourth quarter.
In the case of *śakaṭi* and *śakaṭī*, [the final vowel] is not elided syllable by syllable in alternation (1);
in the case of *goṣṭhaja*, which is a name for a Brāhmaṇa, [the final vowel is not elided] (2);
and in the case of *pārāvata*, with the exception of the penultimate vowel (3).
In the Vedic language (chandas), the words *dhūmra*, *jānu*, *muñja*, *keśa*, *kāla*, *vāla*, *sthālīpāka*, *adhas*, *dhūma*, and *jala* have an acute accent (*udātta*) on their first syllable;
furthermore, the words *kapikeśa* and *harikeśa* also have an acute accent on the first syllable in the Vedic language.
The vowels *nyaṅ* and *svar* are circumflex (*svarita*).

The initial [vowel] of *nyarbuda* and *vyalkaśa* [is long]. (7) The final [vowel] of *tilya*, *śikya*, *matya*, *kārṣmarya*, *dhānya*, *kanya*, *rājanya*, and *manuṣya* [is long]. (8) In the Vedic language (*chandas*), the words *vila*, *abhakṣya*, and *vīrya* [have a long final vowel]. (9)

The words *tvat*, *tvasama*, and *sima* have their final syllable acute; furthermore, in the Atharvaveda, the word *sima* has its final syllable acute. Particles (*nipāta*) have their initial syllable acute.
13. And the prefixes, with the exception of *abhi*. 14. [The final syllable] of words beginning with *eva* is [acute]. 15. Both [syllables] of words beginning with *vāca* are acute.
The particles beginning with *ca* are unaccented (anudātta) [16]. The word *yathā* is unaccented when it occurs at the end of a metrical foot [17],
as is the case in the reduplication of words beginning with *pra* [18].
"Everything else is unaccented (anudātta)"—
this is the fourth quarter of the Phiṭ-sūtras.
